# Project Overview

## Research Question

Can environmental monitoring text predict whether a public health action was taken during a harmful algal bloom (HAB) event?

California HAB bulletins contain unstructured descriptions of bloom conditions, phytoplankton observations, toxin concentrations, marine wildlife impacts, shellfish risk, and public health communication. I use these bulletins to build a text-classification dataset and compare Naive Bayes, Lasso logistic regression, and Random Forest models.

## Data Source and Format

The source data are HTML pages from the [SCCOOS California HAB Bulletin Archive](https://sccoos.org/archive-ca-hab-bulletins/). The original source is unstructured narrative text. I scrape the bulletin pages, convert each bulletin into smaller text segments, and place the text and metadata in a tabular data frame.

The initial scraped corpus has one row per bulletin. The modeling dataset has one row per HAB-relevant text segment and includes the bulletin URL, date information inferred from the title, cleaned predictor text, and a binary public-health-action label.

## Data Access & Cleaning

I use helper functions to clean text, read webpages, and infer dates from bulletin titles and URLs.
